advances: Rules out every integer-centered sublevel of a sum of even convex coordinate costs, and every unimodular affine image of such a sublevel, as a counterexample to the proposed odd-occupied-parity criterion. In this concrete family an occupied class has size at most \((K+1)/2\), which is at most \(K-1\) for \(K\ge3\). This includes arbitrary weighted cross-polytopes and axis-aligned ellipsoids. The unrestricted criterion for complete convex lattice supports remains unresolved.

proof:
Evenness and convexity imply \(\phi_i(t)\ge0\) for every real \(t\), because \(0\) is the midpoint of \(t\) and \(-t\). For \(|t|\ge1\), convexity applied to \(1=(1/|t|)|t|+(1-1/|t|)0\) gives \(\phi_i(t)=\phi_i(|t|)\ge a_i|t|\). Thus the defining real sublevel and its affine image \(C\) are bounded and convex. Consequently \(W\) is finite; it is nonempty because \(\mathbf c\in W\). Since \(C\) is convex and contains \(W\), every integer point of \(\operatorname{conv}(W)\) belongs to \(C\cap\mathbb Z^n=W\). The reverse inclusion is immediate, proving completeness.

The map \(\mathbf z\mapsto\mathbf c+U\mathbf z\) is a bijection of \(\mathbb Z^n\), and its reduction modulo \(2\) is a bijection of parity classes: \(U^{-1}\) has integer entries. It therefore suffices to count classes before this affine change of coordinates. For a subset \(I\subseteq\lbrace1,\ldots,n\rbrace\), write \(\mathbf1_I\) for its coordinate indicator vector. The minimum of \(\sum_j\phi_j(z_j)\) among integer vectors of parity \(\mathbf1_I\) is exactly \(\sum_{j\in I}a_j\). Indeed, every odd coordinate has absolute value at least \(1\), every even coordinate contributes a nonnegative amount, and the minimum is attained by taking coordinates \(\pm1\) on \(I\) and \(0\) off \(I\). Hence the full set of occupied parities, in these coordinates, is exactly

$$
\mathcal F=
\left\lbrace I\subseteq\lbrace1,\ldots,n\rbrace:
\sum_{j\in I}a_j\le R\right\rbrace,
\qquad |\mathcal F|=K.
$$

Choose an index \(i\) with \(a_i=\min_j a_j\). Pair every subset \(I\) not containing \(i\) with \(I\cup\lbrace i\rbrace\). Positivity of \(a_i\) implies that the larger member can belong to \(\mathcal F\) only if the smaller member does. Thus each pair contributes zero, one, or two occupied parities, with a contribution of one occurring precisely when \(I\in\mathcal F\) and \(I\cup\lbrace i\rbrace\notin\mathcal F\). Since \(K\) is odd, at least one such pair exists. Fix its smaller member \(I\), and set \(\delta=R-\sum_{j\in I}a_j\). Then \(0\le\delta<a_i\).

Every integer vector of parity \(\mathbf1_I\) other than the stated sign vectors has either an even coordinate \(z_j\) of absolute value at least \(2\), or an odd coordinate \(z_j\) of absolute value at least \(3\). In the first case that coordinate's cost exceeds its minimum by at least \(2a_j\). In the second case its cost exceeds its minimum by at least \(3a_j-a_j=2a_j\). Every other coordinate has at least its minimum cost. Since \(2a_j\ge2a_i>\delta\), such a vector lies outside the sublevel. Conversely, all \(2^{|I|}\) sign vectors have cost \(\sum_{j\in I}a_j\le R\), so they are the entire class.

The subset \(I\) is nonempty. If it were empty, the unmatched-pair condition would give \(R<a_i\le a_j\) for every \(j\), so only the empty subset would be occupied and \(K=1\), contrary to \(K\ge3\).

Every subset of \(I\) belongs to \(\mathcal F\), giving \(2^{|I|}\) occupied parities that omit \(i\). In addition, for every proper subset \(T\subsetneq I\), choose \(j\in I\setminus T\). Minimality of \(a_i\) gives

$$
\sum_{k\in T}a_k+a_i
\le\sum_{k\in I}a_k-a_j+a_i
\le\sum_{k\in I}a_k
\le R.
$$

Thus \(T\cup\lbrace i\rbrace\) belongs to \(\mathcal F\). These are \(2^{|I|}-1\) additional distinct occupied parities, all containing \(i\). Therefore \(K\ge2^{|I|+1}-1\), proving the asserted size bound. The affine parity bijection transfers the exact class and its cardinality to \(W\).

The family includes weighted cross-polytopes by choosing \(\phi_i(t)=a_i|t|\), and axis-aligned ellipsoids by choosing \(\phi_i(t)=a_it^2\), before the allowed unimodular affine change. No assertion here represents an arbitrary convex lattice support by a separable sublevel. In particular, nonseparable interactions between coordinates are outside the theorem's hypotheses.
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\), let \(\mathbf c\in\mathbb Z^n\), and let \(U\in\mathbb Z^{n\times n}\) have determinant \(1\) or \(-1\). For each \(i\in\lbrace1,\ldots,n\rbrace\), let \(\phi_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be an even convex function satisfying \(\phi_i(0)=0\) and \(a_i:=\phi_i(1)>0\). For \(R\ge0\), define

$$
\begin{aligned}
C&=\mathbf c+U\left\lbrace\mathbf z\in\mathbb R^n:
       \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi_i(z_i)\le R\right\rbrace,\\
W&=C\cap\mathbb Z^n,
\qquad
W_\eta=W\cap(\eta+2\mathbb Z^n)
\quad\bigl(\eta\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace^n\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$

Then \(W\) is finite and nonempty and satisfies \(W=\operatorname{conv}(W)\cap\mathbb Z^n\). Let \(K\) be the number of nonempty classes \(W_\eta\). If \(K\ge3\) is odd, there is a nonempty subset \(I\subseteq\lbrace1,\ldots,n\rbrace\) and an occupied parity class whose points are exactly

$$
\left\lbrace\mathbf c+U\mathbf z:
z_j\in\lbrace-1,1\rbrace\ \text{for }j\in I,
\quad z_j=0\ \text{for }j\notin I\right\rbrace.
$$

Its size is \(2^{|I|}\), and \(2^{|I|+1}-1\le K\). Consequently
\(\min_{\eta:W_\eta\ne\varnothing}|W_\eta|\le(K+1)/2\le K-1\).
